items.title: Oasis Announce 2027 Global Tour Dates
items.summary:
Oasis have confirmed a 2027 tour, ending months of hints from the band on social media and in interviews. The run, titled Oasis Live 27, covers 38 shows across the United Kingdom, Europe and the United States, with Richard Ashcroft opening every date.

The tour begins in May with five nights at Celtic Park in Glasgow, followed by eleven shows at Manchester's Etihad Stadium in June. From there the band move through Munich, Barcelona, Amsterdam, Paris and Rome before crossing to North America in August for three nights at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, and three at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. Two dates at Slane Castle in Ireland precede the finale: four performances at Knebworth Park in September, the site of the band's 1996 festival appearance that Jake Scott later turned into a documentary.

Apart from the Manchester homecoming shows, a press release said the itinerary avoids every location the band played on the 2025 Oasis Live 25 reunion tour, which opened in Cardiff and took in Toronto, Chicago and Los Angeles. That makes Foxborough and Las Vegas first-time stops for the reunited group.

The band marked the announcement with a trailer that opens on archival and reunion footage before "Morning Glory?" arrives and the dates appear. "START THE CELEBRATIONS!!!!" the band said in a statement. "After a period of reflection The Most Damaging Pop Cultural Force In Recent British History has declared itself fit for purpose and will once again return to lift the spirits of the people. Come witness the fitness. It shall be a sight to behold."

Rolling Stone reported that tickets will go only to fans who register in advance through the band's website, with registration closing Thursday, Sept. 17, at 11 a.m. ET. Successful registrants receive a unique, nontransferable code granting access to an assigned on-sale window; U.S. windows differ by city and all fall on Friday, Sept. 25.

The announcement follows the release of Don't Look Back in Anger, a documentary about the reunion created by Peaky Blinders writer Steven Knight and directed by Dylan Southern and Will Lovelace.

items.title: Macklemore Dropped From Ed Sheeran Tour After Onstage ‘Free Palestine’ Statements
items.summary:
Macklemore will not perform on the remaining dates of Ed Sheeran's U.S. Loop Tour after multiple stadiums told the tour's promoter they would not host a show with him on the bill. The removal follows a pair of appearances at MetLife Stadium earlier this month where the rapper called for a free Palestine from the stage.

Messina Touring Group, which promotes the U.S. leg, gave Rolling Stone a statement explaining the decision. "As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran's U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans," the company said. "After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates." He had been booked for eight of the ten shows left, beginning Friday, Sept. 19, in Philadelphia.

In an Instagram statement, Macklemore said Sheeran told him that Patriots and Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft had organized the objection. "Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues," he wrote. Representatives for Kraft and the Kraft Group did not return requests for comment, and neither did reps for Sheeran or most of the venues.

At the Sept. 4 MetLife show, Macklemore projected images of destruction in Gaza and performed "Hind's Hall," his song about the Columbia University protesters who occupied a building and named it for Hind Rajab, a six-year-old killed by the Israeli military. "A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine," he said. The following night he addressed Jewish audience members directly, saying criticism of Israel was "in no way" a criticism of them.

The backlash arrived quickly. StopAntisemitism accused him of ambushing fans with anti-Israel propaganda in a post Pink shared, and the Israeli American Council circulated a petition asking Sheeran to drop him. Pink later clarified her position, writing, "I have never asked for another artist to be silenced and I'm not asking now. I don't need anyone fired, and I don't need a refund."

The venues named include Lincoln Financial Field, Gillette Stadium, Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Lucas Oil Stadium, Bank of America Stadium, AT&T Stadium and Raymond James Stadium. Only two of them are privately owned; the rest belong to cities, states or other government bodies, which could raise First Amendment questions if the exclusion turned on the rapper's remarks. Raymond James Stadium hosted two Kanye West concerts earlier this summer despite similar calls for cancellation, after West's promoter wrote a clause into the contract barring the venue from pulling the shows.

items.title: ‘Industry’ Adds Ben Platt, Russell Tovey to Final Season Cast
items.summary:
Ben Platt and Russell Tovey have joined the cast of Industry for its fifth and final season, which is currently filming in the United Kingdom. Both actors take guest roles on the HBO and BBC drama.

Platt, whose credits include The Beauty and Dear Evan Hansen, plays Matt Crenshaw, a venture capitalist who backed a wellness tech company early. The Hollywood Reporter noted that the character descriptions for Zosia Mamet and Dianna Agron's roles also reference a wellness tech company, suggesting the three storylines intersect. Tovey, known for Years and Years and Feud: Capote vs. the Swans, plays Declan P. Davis, an aide to left-wing politician Nikesh Shah, played by Bally Gill.

They join a sizable group of season five arrivals that also includes Cary Elwes, Sam Riley, Jessica Brown Findlay, Luke Manley and Eduard Poliakov. Season four closed with professional and personal disruption for several of the show's regulars, whose ranks included Myha'la, Marisa Abela, Kit Harington, Ken Leung, Max Minghella, Kiernan Shipka and Kal Penn.

Mickey Down and Konrad Kay created the series and continue to write and direct it. They executive produce alongside Jane Tranter, Kate Crowther and Ryan Rasmussen for Bad Wolf, Kathleen McCaffrey for Little Gems, and Rebecca Ferguson for the BBC.

items.title: Jeff Tweedy, Robert Glasper, Weyes Blood to Play Big Ears 2027
items.summary:
Big Ears has announced the lineup for its 2027 edition, which runs April 1 through 4 across downtown Knoxville, Tennessee. Jeff Tweedy, Robert Glasper, Weyes Blood, Oneohtrix Point Never, Bill Frisell and Dinner Party — the quartet of Glasper, Terrace Martin, Kamasi Washington and 9th Wonder — sit at the top of the bill.

The festival will stage more than 250 performances across two dozen venues. Also booked are Thundercat, Wednesday, Natalie Merchant, Mavis Staples, Courtney Barnett, Sylvan Esso, Jim James, Kevin Morby, Norah Jones, Mount Eerie, L'Rain, Gillian Welch and David Rawlings, Meat Puppets, Andy Stott, Midori Takada, Kali Malone, Valerie June and Jeff Parker, among many others.

Further down the schedule are an orchestral performance of David Bowie's Blackstar and a twelve-hour set of Indian classical music, alongside sets from Nirosta Steel, Ana Roxanne, Marina Herlop, Horse Lords, SML, Joanne Robertson, Otto Benson, Avey Tare, Carla dal Forno, Dagmar Zuniga, Ida and Helen.

Now in its 14th year, Big Ears has built its identity around "Deep Listening," the concept coined by electronic composer Pauline Oliveros. Writing for Pitchfork in 2019, Andrew Frisicano credited the Knoxville event with helping push festival programming toward tightly curated, if rarely short, lineups organized around meditative experiences.

items.title: Dead Boys Guitarist Cheetah Chrome Dies at 71
items.summary:
Eugene Richard O'Connor, the guitarist who performed as Cheetah Chrome and helped found the Dead Boys, died Sunday at 71. His bandmates confirmed the death in an Instagram post.

"Cheetah was a true original, an architect of the punk rock movement," the band wrote. "A one-man hurricane tearing up the musical landscape with his feral guitar riffs and manic energy. Beyond all that Cheetah was also just a really sweet guy that loved rock-roll." The post, signed by Tony, Chris, Mark and the Dead Boys family, asked for privacy and closed with "Godspeed Cheetah."

Born in Cleveland and later based in Nashville, O'Connor joined Rocket from the Tombs as a guitarist in 1974 before forming Frankenstein with Stiv Bators and Johnny Blitz. That group became the Dead Boys, who released Young, Loud and Snotty in 1977 and We Have Come for Your Children the following year before splitting in 1979.

Variety reported that the band regrouped for live dates over the years but never recorded another studio album. They had been planning a 2027 tour built around the 50th anniversary of their debut. O'Connor is survived by his wife, Anna O'Connor, and their 14-year-old son, Rogan, both of Nashville.
